name: Santa María Zacatepec Mixtec
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Checked Towne 2011 'Gramatica popular del tacuate (mixteco) de Santa Maria Zacatepec' full PDF (Internet Archive copy of SIL GS12b): only tone and orthographic accent-for-tone are described; no word-stress statement found.

sources.citation: Towne, Douglas. 2011. Gramática popular del tacuate (mixteco) de Santa María Zacatepec, Oaxaca. (Serie gramáticas de lenguas indígenas de México 12.) México, D.F.: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. vii+140 pp. (electronic edition May 2012, downloaded via the Internet Archive from www-01.sil.org)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Ch. 2 'El alfabeto tacuate' (pp. 5-10) covers vowels (plain, long, 'cortadas' = glottalized, nasalized), three level tones and their lexical/grammatical functions, consonants, loans; no statement of where word stress falls. Only accent-related remark is p. 97 (§12.2): enclitic adverbs -ni 'nada más' and -ga 'más' 'no tiene acento propio' and are therefore written attached to the preceding word. 'acento' elsewhere = orthographic diacritics for tone.

sources.citation: Peña Flores, Esmeralda & Pafnuncio Antonio Ramos. 2025. Frases nominales simples en tuʹun vaʹa (mixteco) de Santa María Zacatepec. RASAL Lingüística 2025(2): 53-80. doi:10.56683/rs252163
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp. 56-58: brief phonological profile (18 consonants, 5 vowels, vowel types, three level tones + rising/falling contours with minimal pairs); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Peña Flores, Esmeralda. 2023. Frases nominales en tu'un va'a (mixteco) de Santa María Zacatepec, Oaxaca. Tesis de maestría, Universidad de Sonora (Hermosillo). 155 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §2.3.1-2.3.2 (pp. 33-38): consonant and vowel inventory, open syllables only, modal vs non-modal (glottalized/rearticulated) vowels, three level tones plus contour tones, tonal aspect marking on first syllable of verb root. No mention of stress/acento (the word 'acento' occurs only for tone diacritics).

sources.citation: Peña Flores, Esmeralda. 2020. Frases nominales en español de hablantes bilingües tacuate-español de Santa María Zacatepec, Oaxaca. Tesis de licenciatura, Benemérita Universidad Autónoma de Puebla. 192 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 39-40: short summary of Tacuate vowels and tones taken from Towne 2011; nothing on Tacuate stress (only Spanish plural allomorphy mentions 'vocal con acento').

sources.citation: Penner, Kevin L. 2019. Prosodic structure in Ixtayutla Mixtec: Evidence for the foot. PhD dissertation, University of Alberta. (describes Ixtayutla Mixtec, ixta1235/vmj, the neighbouring variety Towne also calls 'tacuate')
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Checked only for Zacatepec mentions: cites Zacatepec Mixtec (Josserand 1983; Towne 2011) solely for couplet-final glottalized vowels (fn. 5 p. 65, fn. 17 p. 253); says nothing about Zacatepec stress. Its own stress analysis concerns Ixtayutla Mixtec, a different glottocode.

sources.citation: McKendry, Inga. 2013. Tonal association, prominence and prosodic structure in South-eastern Nochixtlán Mixtec. PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Santa María Zacatepec [mza] appears only in Appendix B (list of Ethnologue codes); no data or stress statement for this variety.

sources.citation: Secretaría de Cultura / INALI. 2022. Norma de escritura del Tu'un Savi (idioma mixteco). México: INALI.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Pan-Mixtec orthographic norm cited by Peña Flores for the Zacatepec inventory; may contain a generic statement on Mixtec word accent, though not variety-specific.

sources.citation: Consejo de Ancianos de Santa María Zacatepec (in preparation, reported by Peña Flores 2020: 39 fn. 12). Diccionario bilingüe tacuate-español.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Community bilingual dictionary said to be in preparation; if published with a grammatical/orthographic introduction it could contain an accent statement.

sources.citation: Josserand, Judy Kathryn. 1983. Mixtec Dialect History (Proto-Mixtec and Modern Mixtec Text). PhD dissertation, Tulane University.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Pan-Mixtec dialect survey that includes Zacatepec wordlist data (cited for Zacatepec by Penner 2019 and Peña Flores); contains general statements on Mixtec couplet stress and may transcribe Zacatepec forms with stress — the only older primary source likely to say anything about prominence in this variety.
